newsitem.title: CHILE: EU vice-president Leon Brittan to visit Chile.
newsitem.headline: EU vice-president Leon Brittan to visit Chile.

text.p: European Union (EU) commission vice-president Leon Brittan will make a four-day official visit to Chile at the end of the month, aimed at boosting trade ties, said EU representative Kurt Juul on Wednesday.
"Mr. Brittan has heard a great deal about Chile as an emerging country," Juul told reporters after a meeting with Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza.
"He is very interested in the seeing the reality of an emerging country in America."
Chile and the EU signed an economic co-operation pact at the EU summit in Florence in June, which Chile hopes to eventually extend to a full free trade agreement.
The bloc is one of Chile's largest trading partners, with bilateral trade totalling $7.6 billion in 1995.
Brittan, who is in charge of the EU's trade relations, will arrive in Chile March 28 on a private weekend visit to the far southern Patagonian region.
He begins his four-day official visit on March 31 and then leaves for Brazil.
